narrative.overview:
Spinbox is set like a radio listings magazine for one household's evening. The record turns on a night-blue deck. The pages are newsprint paper, divided by ink rules. The queue is a timetable that shows when each Track will air. Every surface is either **night** (the rail, the deck, the mini-dock, auth) or **paper** (the pages and the listing). The two meet at a hard edge, with no gradient between them.

Type does the work that imagery and chrome do in a streaming app. Titles are condensed Archivo at weight 800 in uppercase, set tight like a magazine masthead. Body copy stays at normal width so it reads easily. Times and durations use tabular figures, so the listing reads like a printed schedule. Colour is rationed. Red means only that something is live. Yellow means only "this one, now". Every other colour is quarantined to the artwork plates.

The world is flat and square. There are no rounded cards, glows or decorative gradients. Depth comes from the night/paper split, 3px and 2px ink rules, 1.5px ink borders and hairline row dividers. The only circles are things that are physically round: the record, its label, the spindle, the transport play button and the plate play button.
keyCharacteristics: Night-blue chrome (rail, deck, mini-dock, tabs, auth) against warm paper pages.
Condensed uppercase Archivo 800 for titles; normal-width Archivo for reading.
Square corners everywhere except physically round objects.
Ink rules as structure: 3px under page heads and above listings, 2px above section titles, hairlines between rows.
Red only for live state; yellow only for current and selection.
Tabular-figure clocks and durations: the queue is a timetable.
The spinning record with tonearm is the centrepiece of Now playing.

rules.name: The On-Air Rule
rules.body: Red marks live state and nothing else. Use it for the on-air tag, the lamps, the wordmark dot and the record label. Errors use a 1.5px red-ink border and a red-ink icon on sheet or paper, never a red fill.

rules.name: The Highlighter Rule
rules.body: Yellow means "this one, now": the current listing row, the current rail item, the current mobile tab, text selection, and hover on the item about to be chosen. It never decorates.

rules.name: The Plate Quarantine Rule
rules.body: Colour outside red and yellow lives only inside artwork plates. A generated sleeve may use any of five colourways: night, red ink, yellow, ink or paper-deep. The surrounding chrome never borrows a plate's colour.

rules.name: The Masthead Rule
rules.body: Titles are condensed (68% width), weight 800 and uppercase, with line-height ≤ 1. Body copy is never condensed and never uppercase.

rules.name: The Timetable Rule
rules.body: Every number that a reader scans down a column uses tabular figures at semi-condensed width.

rules.name: The Small Caps Carry State Rule
rules.body: Small uppercase caps label a state (on air, paused, can't play, missing, admin, disabled) or a time. They never sit above a heading as an introduction.

rules.name: The Flat Stock Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Only floating overlays cast a soft shadow, and it is always ink-tinted and offset downward or outward, never a glow.

rules.name: The Layer Order Rule
rules.body: Remix `css()` emits each class into its own sublayer, `@layer rmx.<hash>`, and orders the sublayers by first appearance in the document. `globalStyles` declares `@layer reset, rmx;` first and keeps every element reset inside `@layer reset`, because unlayered global CSS would beat every `css()` style. In `mix={[base, modifier]}`, a modifier wins only if its layer was created after the base's. A shared modifier can therefore lose, so it sets custom properties that the base reads. For example, `btnSmall` sets `--btn-h`, `--btn-px` and `--btn-fs`, and `buttonBase` consumes them. Surface tones work the same way: `paperTone` and `nightTone` set `--tx-fg`, `--tx-bg`, `--tx-mute` and `--tx-rest`. Nested selectors on a parent class (for example `'& h2'`) can lose to a later layer, so style the child directly.

rules.name: The Inline-Flex Icon Rule
rules.body: Icon buttons centre their glyph with `display: inline-flex`, never grid. A hidden label inside a grid creates a phantom row.

rules.name: The String Clamp Rule
rules.body: Unitless properties passed to `css()` must be strings. Write `WebkitLineClamp: '2'`, because the number `2` compiles to `2px`.

rules.name: The Square-Stroke Icon Rule
rules.body: Icons are inline 24×24 SVGs with a 2px `currentColor` stroke, square caps and miter joins. Transport glyphs use solid fills. Size them with CSS (1–1.5rem), never with an icon font.

dos: **Do** set every title in condensed (68% width) Archivo 800 uppercase with line-height ≤ 1, and keep reading text at normal width.
**Do** mark structure with ink rules: 3px under page heads and above listings, 2px above section titles, and 1px rule between rows.
**Do** keep red for live state (the on-air tag, lamps, the record label) and draw errors as a 1.5px red-ink border with a red-ink icon on sheet or paper.
**Do** keep yellow for the current row, the current rail item, the current tab, selection, and hover on the item about to be chosen.
**Do** use tabular figures at 82% width for clocks, durations and counts.
**Do** keep corners square. Reserve 50% radius for objects that are physically round.
**Do** make a shared modifier set custom properties that the base reads, instead of overriding properties directly.
**Do** keep every control at least 2.75rem tall and collapse all motion under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
donts: **Don't** use red fills for errors or decoration, or yellow for anything other than "current" or "selected".
**Don't** round cards, buttons, inputs or plates.
**Don't** add glows, decorative gradients or resting shadows. The only gradients render the record.
**Don't** put a small uppercase eyebrow or kicker above a heading. Small caps carry state or time only.
**Don't** let chrome borrow a plate's colourway. Colour stays inside the plate.
**Don't** write global element CSS outside `@layer reset`, or pass numbers for unitless `css()` properties.
